item.title: Scaling Microservices at Mach Speed
item.description: When our client came to us, their monolithic application was buckling under the weight of success. What started as a fintech MVP serving 10,000 requests per day had grown to the breaking point. They needed to scale to millions of daily requests—and they needed to do it yesterday. The Challenge: Growing Pains at Scale The symptoms were all too familiar: Response times degrading from 200ms to 2+ seconds under load Database connections maxing out during peak hours Deployment windows stretching to hours with increasing rollback rates Development velocity grinding to a halt as teams stepped on each other’s toes The monolith had served them well during the startup phase, but it was time for a fundamental architectural shift.

item.title: Building Culture in Remote Engineering Teams
item.description: When the world went remote in 2020, many thought it would be temporary. Four years later, remote work has become the norm for engineering teams. But building culture remotely? That’s still a challenge many teams struggle with. Over the past few years, we’ve helped dozens of engineering teams build thriving remote cultures. Here’s what actually works. The Culture Challenge Remote work solves many problems but creates new ones: Isolation: Engineers feeling disconnected from their team Communication gaps: Important context lost in translation Timezone friction: Half the team is always asleep Onboarding struggles: New hires taking months to feel integrated The traditional solution—more meetings—often makes things worse.

item.title: Legacy Modernization Without Tears
item.description: “We need to rewrite everything from scratch.” Those six words have killed more engineering teams than any bug ever could. After modernizing dozens of legacy systems, we’ve learned that the rewrite is rarely the answer. Here’s our battle-tested approach to breathing new life into old code. The Reality of Legacy Let’s be honest about what we’re dealing with: A Java 6 monolith that processes $10M daily 500K lines of code, half without tests The original developers have long moved on Documentation exists… somewhere It works, but nobody knows exactly how Sound familiar?
